book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Camping out — or sailing?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sleeping in a tent
second meaning: moving with sails set, as a ship once carried sheets of heavy cloth

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker weighs up a tent against a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Canvas is both tent fabric and old sailcloth, so a ship under full canvas is under sail.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means sheltered by a tent and also, in nautical idiom, with sails spread.

clue.text: Old city features ragged children

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city
chins are facial features

explanation.surface: An ancient city's ruins show scruffy kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' looks like a verb meaning includes; it is the noun, parts of a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Urchins are poor, scruffily dressed children of the streets.

clue.text: Sort of lead mother will follow in principle

indicators.note: says the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a dog lead is a sort of lead
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A kind of leadership that has the mother following it as a matter of principle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a firmly held tenet, a principle laid down as true.

clue.text: Kick up a fuss, as Adam and Eve had to do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for making a loud commotion

definitions.text: as Adam and Eve had to do
definitions.meaning: second meaning: they had to bring up their first son

explanation.surface: Making a scene, as the first couple were forced to.
explanation.walkthrough: To raise a child is to bring them up, and Cain was Adam and Eve's elder son.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cause trouble noisily, and literally describes rearing Genesis's first-born.

clue.text: A grate not fully closed

parts.note: taken as written
to jar is to grate, as a noise grates on the nerves

explanation.surface: A fireplace grate that has not been shut properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grate' reads as the iron basket in a fireplace; it is the verb, to rasp or irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is slightly open, so it is not completely shut.

clue.text: They're old soldiers entering wrong events

definitions.note: a clause standing for a plural noun: those who are old

indicators.note: the troops go inside the other letters
something wrong is out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: Former soldiers turning up at the wrong functions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old soldiers' wants to be the definition, but 'soldiers' is the regiment going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans are people long experienced or long-serving, and so typically older.

clue.text: More than one team takes part

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the opposing teams in a match
second meaning: a verb, supports one party in a dispute

explanation.surface: Several teams join in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means teams, and as a verb, to side with someone is to take their part.

clue.text: Security is lifted in the store

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the place that follows

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word makes it read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned upwards

explanation.surface: Goods are being stolen from inside the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' looks like shoplifted, and 'security' like guards; it is a sum held as a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is money paid as a pledge or guarantee, a form of security.

clue.text: Well done! A fine performance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old-fashioned British cry of approval
second meaning: an impressive display

explanation.surface: Applause after an excellent performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a dated exclamation of praise and a description of a creditable effort.

clue.text: Aware of son acting badly

indicators.note: acting badly suggests a performance gone wrong, so the letters before it are scrambled

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A parent realises their boy has been misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cognisant of something is a formal synonym for knowing of it.

clue.text: Number receive poor return and become dejected

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone gets a bad result and loses heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure, but here it is the Roman numeral 500, D.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or flag, used figuratively of spirits sinking.

clue.text: Is the first murder victim a girl?

parts.note: taken as written
in Genesis, Abel was killed by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether Genesis's first victim was female.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a woman's given name, an example of a name for a girl.

clue.text: Struggles to maintain faith in the past

definitions.meaning: surface reading: someone finding it hard to keep believing
setter's reading: medieval holy wars fought to uphold Christianity

explanation.surface: A believer has wrestled with doubt over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval campaigns to the Holy Land were wars waged in defence of Christian belief.

clue.text: Oriental vessel is a mile in length

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the word that follows

parts.note: a span is a length or extent
M is the abbreviation for mile
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eastern ship is said to measure a whole mile long.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in China and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Lunar settlement?

parts.note: surface reading: a colony or base built on the moon; setter's reading: fine powder that has settled on the moon's surface

explanation.surface: A colony on the moon, as science fiction imagines.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon's surface is coated in fine regolith, the grit that has settled there over ages.

clue.text: Picture may take a goalkeeper by surprise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quick informal photograph

definitions.text: may take a goalkeeper by surprise
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a sudden strike at goal with no build-up

explanation.surface: A sports photographer's image catches a keeper unawares.
explanation.walkthrough: As two words, a snap shot is football slang for a quick unexpected shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a casual photograph, and in football a hurried shot that catches the keeper unready.

clue.text: Outstanding piece of cinematic apparatus?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that juts out
second meaning: the machine that throws film onto a screen

explanation.surface: A superb bit of film equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like excellent; it means standing out, protruding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the machine casting images on a screen, and literally a thing that sticks out.

clue.text: Widely shown film of American disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruin, so the word before it is broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A disaster movie about an American catastrophe gets a wide release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Widely shown' suggests a wide release; it means a wide screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinerama was a 1950s widescreen process projecting film across a huge curved screen.

clue.text: Proverbially, no longer a stud

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: the large-headed nail studding old doors, proverbially dead
surface reading: a breeding stallion that has been retired

explanation.surface: A retired stallion is spoken of as past it.
explanation.walkthrough: A stud is also a large-headed nail; the saying 'dead as a doornail' makes this one proverbially lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A doornail is a stud-like nail on a door, and the proverb holds it to be the deadest thing.

clue.text: Excursion ending at nightfall

definitions.meaning: surface reading: an outing of some kind
setter's reading: one that is over within the daylight hours

explanation.surface: An outing that wraps up when darkness comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pleasure trip that leaves and returns within the daylight hours.

clue.text: Dangerous to fly, use horse and trap

definitions.note: an adjective phrase for a noun: the thing that is a danger to a fly

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
a spider's web is a trap

explanation.surface: A warning against flying, recommending a pony and two-wheeled cart instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse and trap' reads as a carriage, and 'fly' as travel by air; the fly is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's silk net catches insects, so it is a peril to any fly.

clue.text: It's a fixed sort of charge

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: the blade soldiers fix to rifles before charging the enemy
surface reading: a set fee that does not vary

explanation.surface: A flat-rate fee, as on a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Infantry 'fix bayonets' before an attack, so the charge is a military assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The blade fastened to a rifle muzzle is fixed in place for an infantry assault.

clue.text: He may give you an off-peak call

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: a mountain singer whose warbling cry rings out from the peaks
surface reading: a phone call made at the cheap time of day

explanation.surface: Someone rings you when telephone rates are cheaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-peak is British for outside the busy, expensive hours; here the call comes off an actual mountain peak.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine singer warbles a cry between chest voice and falsetto, traditionally sent across the mountains.

clue.text: Famous composer? Hear, hear

indicators.note: the second hear asks us to go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: list is an archaic word meaning to listen or hear

explanation.surface: A shout of approval for a celebrated musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear, hear' looks like applause; the first is the archaic verb list, the second the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the celebrated nineteenth-century Hungarian pianist and composer.

clue.text: There's your hidden error

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked inside other words, so look within the words before it

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone points out a mistake that was concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is doctrinal error, a belief contrary to accepted teaching.

clue.text: Provide some point to a joke

parts.note: E is east, one of the compass points
a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Advice to make a joke sharper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like the punchline of the joke; it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish or supply with what is needed.

clue.text: He floated a company to avoid liquidation

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: the patriarch whose ark kept a company of animals afloat through the Flood

definitions.text: floated a company to avoid liquidation
definitions.meaning: surface reading: a businessman launched a firm on the stock market to stave off insolvency

explanation.surface: A businessman takes his firm public to escape bankruptcy.
explanation.walkthrough: Floating, company and liquidation all read as finance; they are the ark, the animals and the deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch built the ark and carried his family and the animals safely through the Flood.

clue.text: Sprays of flowers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the perforated nozzles on watering cans that spray water
second meaning: blooms of a thorny garden shrub

explanation.surface: Bunches of blooms, as a florist would sell them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprays of flowers' reads as bouquets; the spray is the sprinkler head on a watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprinkler head of a watering can shares its name with the classic garden bloom.

clue.text: A call for military revolution

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: a parade-ground command that has soldiers spin to face the other way
surface reading: a summons to an army uprising

explanation.surface: Someone urges the army to rise up against the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' is a turn of the body, not a coup.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill order turns troops through half a circle, a literal revolution on the parade ground.

clue.text: Treat speech as showing bias in class

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the favoured pupil, the object of that bias

indicators.note: the letters are put on show in a fresh order

parts.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A speech therapist's lesson seems to favour some pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat' looks like the verb doing the work, but it is part of the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a favourite pupil, the embodiment of a teacher's partiality in the classroom.
